content.title: ESPN Unlimited Unveils 2026 MLB Game of the Day Schedule With Early Spring Lineup | Cord Cutters News
content.text: For the 2026 season, baseball fans will have a steady stream of must-watch matchups after the MLB Game of the Day on ESPN Unlimited schedule was unveiled through May. The action on the field begins on Opening Day and features all 30 clubs with some of the sport’s biggest stars front and center. Global sensation Shohei Ohtani, Yankees slugger Aaron Judge, rising star Bobby Witt Jr., and Phillies standout Bryce Harper will all be available to watch for ESPN Unlimited subscribers on the ESPN app. The action begins on March 26 with the Texas Rangers visiting the Philadelphia Phillies, setting the tone for what ESPN is positioning as a daily destination for out-of-market baseball. Opening weekend continues with several high-profile matchups, including the New York Yankees taking on the San Francisco Giants on March 27. Aaron Judge leads the Yankees’ lineup in an early test against a National League contender. The springtime lineup features matchups between playoff-caliber teams, division rivalries, and MVP-level talent. Announced games involving Shohei Ohtani and the Dodgers, as well as multiple Yankees appearances led by Aaron Judge, give this early schedule serious star power. MLB.TV on ESPN Changes the Streaming Game This season also marks a major shift for baseball streaming. MLB.TV is now integrated directly into ESPN, making the ESPN App a central hub for out-of-market games. Fans who subscribe to MLB.TV through ESPN can stream thousands of live games, access on-demand replays, and watch MLB Big Inning and MLB Network content, all in one place. The platform also includes features like multiview, live stats, and key play tracking, giving viewers a more interactive experience. Pricing starts at $149.99 for the full season or $29.99 per month, with a discounted seasonal rate available for ESPN Unlimited subscribers. New MLB.TV subscribers also get a one-month free trial of ESPN Unlimited, adding even more value for cord cutters. For fans looking to ditch cable without missing the season, ESPN Unlimited has positioned itself as a go-to for MLB fans. The combination of exclusive daily games and full MLB.TV access means fewer apps, fewer logins, and more baseball in one place. There are still blackout restrictions to consider, especially for local teams, but the overall experience is far more streamlined than in previous seasons. With the early MLB Game of the Day schedule, ESPN is delivering big teams, superstar players, and meaningful matchups right out of the gate. You can check out the full announced schedule below.
